newsitem.title: FRANCE: Russia has most prisoners in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Russia has most prisoners in Europe.

text.p: Russia has by far the highest percentage of detainees in Europe and Sweden has the most escape-prone prisons, according to annual statistics released by the Council of Europe on Thursday.
It said Russia had 694 people in jail for every 100,000 citizens, way ahead of Ukraine's 392 and Lithuania's 356.
Figures were much lower in western Europe, with 122.4 in Spain, 99.3 in Britain, 89 in France, 87 in Italy, 81 in Germany, 80.8 in Switzerland and 75.7 in Belgium.
Cyprus with 26.3 and Slovenia with 24.1 came bottom of the list.
Statistics were not available for about 10 of the Council's 40 members countries including Poland, Greece and the Netherlands.
Romanian prisons were the most overcrowded with 151 detainees for 100 berths.

The rate of pre-trial detention was highest in Belgium, Romania, Italy and France where more than 40 percent of detainees were awaiting trial. It was lowest at nine percent in Ireland and five percent in Iceland.
Finland and Scotland had the highest prison suicide rates -- 30 and 29 suicides per 10,000 detainees respectively.
Sweden topped the escape list, reporting that 220 of every 10,000 inmates had vanished.
